easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak in these verses?
easy.explanation: The first verse begins: “And the Lord said unto Abram.”

easy.question: What did the Lord command Abram to leave?

easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Abram to leave his country, his kindred, and his father’s house.

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says: “And I will make of thee a great nation.”

Abram receives a land, and then is commanded to leave
The Lord blesses all families, and then speaks with Abram

Because all families of the earth would be blessed through him

easy.question: How old was Abram when he left Haran?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

easy.question: To which land did Abram and his people go?
easy.explanation: They set out for the land of Canaan and arrived there.

medium.question: What does “Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him” show?
answers: Abram acted according to the Lord’s command
medium.explanation: The phrase shows that Abram heard the Lord’s command and carried it out.

medium.question: What does “all their substance” mean in this context?
answers: The possessions and goods they had
The people they met along the way

answers: They arrived in Canaan, gathered their possessions, and then left
They left Haran, stayed there, and then returned
They took their family and possessions, departed, and arrived in Canaan

answers: The journey included a whole group, not Abram alone
challenge.explanation: The list of people and possessions shows that Abram traveled with his family and others.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “the souls that they had gotten in Haran” emphasize?
answers: That all the people were born in Canaan
That Abram and his people had others who joined them or were under their care
That Abram built houses in Haran
challenge.explanation: In the context of taking their family and possessions, the phrase refers to people connected with Abram’s household who traveled with him.

paragraphs.title: Arrival in the Land and Building Altars

easy.question: Where did Abram arrive in the land?
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that Abram came to the place of Sichem.

easy.question: What did the Lord promise to give Abram’s seed?
easy.explanation: The Lord said to Abram: “Unto thy seed will I give this land.”

easy.question: What did Abram build for the Lord?
easy.explanation: After the Lord appeared to him, Abram built an altar to the Lord.

medium.question: What did Abram do after the Lord appeared to him and promised him the land?
answers: He built an altar to the Lord
medium.explanation: Following the Lord’s appearance and promise, Abram built an altar to Him.

medium.question: What does “he removed from thence” mean in this context?
answers: He moved or continued to another place
medium.explanation: The verse shows that Abram moved from the previous place toward the mountain.

medium.question: What did Abram do after moving to the mountain, according to the order of the verse?
medium.explanation: The verse first says that Abram moved to the mountain, and then that he pitched his tent.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the location of Abram’s tent between Bethel and Hai?
answers: He camped in the area between the two places
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Bethel was on the west and Hai on the east, so his tent was between them.

challenge.question: To whom does “who appeared unto him” refer in verse 7?
answers: The Canaanite who was in the land
The Lord who appeared to Abram
challenge.explanation: The phrase follows the statement that the Lord appeared to Abram, so it refers to the Lord.

challenge.question: What idea is emphasized by Abram building altars and calling on the Lord’s name at different places?
answers: He wanted to establish an army
He wanted to get away from everyone
Worship of the Lord accompanied him on his journey
challenge.explanation: Abram built altars at Sichem and near Bethel and called on the Lord’s name, showing that worship accompanied his journey.

easy.question: Who journeyed in this verse?

easy.question: In which direction did Abram travel?
easy.explanation: Abram continued toward the south.

easy.question: What action is described in the verse?
easy.explanation: The verse describes Abram’s journey.

medium.question: What does “going on still” show about Abram’s journey?
answers: He continued moving from place to place
medium.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that Abram remained in motion and continued his journey.

medium.question: What does “toward the south” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: The verse says that Abram traveled southward.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events in the verse?
answers: Abram stopped and then began walking
Abram built a city and then journeyed
Abram journeyed and continued moving southward
medium.explanation: The verse describes Abram journeying and continuing toward the south.

challenge.explanation: The phrase adds the idea that Abram continued and persevered in his journey.

challenge.question: What does the verse not explicitly say about Abram?
answers: That he reached his final destination
challenge.explanation: The verse describes his journey toward the south but does not say that he had already reached his destination.

challenge.question: What detail shows that Abram continued traveling rather than stopping?
answers: The statement that he was still going on
The fact that he had a tent
challenge.explanation: The phrase “going on still” directly indicates that Abram continued traveling.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “going on still” rather than simply “Abram journeyed”?
questions.explanation: The phrase adds the idea that Abram continued and persevered in his journey.

questions.question: What does the verse not explicitly say about Abram?
answers: That he reached his final destination

paragraphs.title: The Famine and the Journey Down to Egypt

easy.question: What was in the land?
easy.explanation: The verse says: “And there was a famine in the land.”

easy.question: Where did Abram go down?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Abram went down into Egypt.

easy.question: What did Abram intend to do in Egypt?
easy.explanation: Abram went down into Egypt “to sojourn there.”

medium.question: Why did Abram go down into Egypt?
answers: Because he wanted to wage war
Because he was commanded to build an altar
medium.explanation: The verse explains that Abram went to Egypt because the famine in the land was severe.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Abram went to Egypt, and then the famine began
There was a famine, and Abram went to Egypt to sojourn there
Abram built a city, and then went to Egypt
medium.explanation: The verse first describes the famine and then Abram’s journey to Egypt.

medium.question: What does “to sojourn there” mean?
answers: To stay there for a time
medium.explanation: To sojourn means to stay or live in a place temporarily; Abram went to Egypt during the famine.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the mention of the famine and the words “the famine was grievous”?
answers: The famine lasted only one day
The famine was only in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The description emphasizes that the famine was very severe.

challenge.question: What is the role of “for” in the verse?
answers: It explains the reason Abram went to Egypt
It describes the place to which he went
challenge.explanation: “For” connects Abram’s journey to Egypt with its reason: the severe famine.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “to sojourn there”?
answers: Abram planned to remain in Egypt forever
His stay in Egypt was probably temporary
challenge.explanation: The word “sojourn” describes a stay in a place rather than a permanent move, suggesting a temporary stay.

easy.question: Where was Abram approaching?

easy.question: What was Sarai to Abram?

easy.question: What did Abram ask Sarai to say?
easy.explanation: Abram asked her to say: “Thou art my sister.”

medium.question: Why was Abram afraid that the Egyptians would kill him?
answers: Because Sarai was beautiful and they would want her
Because he had taken their possessions
Because he refused to speak with them
medium.explanation: Abram feared that the Egyptians would see Sarai’s beauty, want her, and kill him.

medium.question: What does “come near to enter” mean in this context?
medium.explanation: In the context of entering Egypt, the phrase means that Abram was approaching Egypt.

medium.question: What did Abram fear would happen if the Egyptians thought Sarai was his wife?
answers: They would drive them both away
They would kill Abram and let Sarai live
They would send them back to Canaan
medium.explanation: Abram said: “they will kill me, but they will save thee alive.”

challenge.question: What did Abram hope to achieve by presenting Sarai as his sister?
answers: To survive and receive favor because of her
To conceal that he was from Egypt
challenge.explanation: Abram hoped that he would live and be treated well because of Sarai.

challenge.question: What contrast appears in Abram’s words about Sarai?
answers: He calls her his sister, although she is his wife
He calls her his mother, although she is his daughter
He calls her his daughter, although she is his sister
challenge.explanation: The passage presents Sarai as Abram’s wife, but Abram asks her to say that she is his sister.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the words “my soul shall live because of thee”?
answers: Abram thought Sarai would deliberately endanger him
Abram asked Sarai to protect him from a war
Abram saw presenting her as his sister as a way to save his life
challenge.explanation: The words show that Abram’s main purpose was to remain alive.

easy.question: What did the Egyptians see about the woman?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Egyptians saw that the woman was very fair.

easy.question: Who praised the woman before Pharaoh?
easy.explanation: The verse says: “The princes also of Pharaoh saw her, and commended her before Pharaoh.”

easy.question: What did Abram receive as a result of these events?
easy.explanation: The verse lists sheep, oxen, asses, menservants, maidservants, she-asses, and camels.

medium.question: Why did Pharaoh’s princes tell Pharaoh about the woman?
answers: Because they saw that she was very beautiful
Because she asked them for help
medium.explanation: They saw her beauty and then commended her before Pharaoh.

medium.question: What does “commended her before Pharaoh” mean?
answers: They praised her and spoke well of her
medium.explanation: The context shows that they praised the woman before Pharaoh after noticing her beauty.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The woman was taken to Pharaoh’s house, and then the Egyptians saw her
Abram received camels, and then Pharaoh saw the woman
The Egyptians saw the woman, Pharaoh’s princes praised her, and she was taken to Pharaoh’s house
medium.explanation: This is the sequence described in verses 14–15.

challenge.question: To whom does “for her sake” refer in “he entreated Abram well for her sake”?
answers: The woman who was taken to Pharaoh’s house
challenge.explanation: The phrase follows the account of the woman being taken, so Abram was treated well because of her.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from the connection between verses 15 and 16?
answers: Pharaoh treated Abram well because of the woman
Pharaoh’s princes gave their possessions to the woman
challenge.explanation: The verse says Abram was treated well “for her sake” and then lists the possessions he received.

challenge.question: What was the practical result of the woman’s beauty according to these verses?
answers: She attracted the Egyptians’ attention and was taken to Pharaoh’s house

answers: She attracted the Egyptians’ attention and was taken to Pharaoh’s house

paragraphs.title: The Plagues and the Departure from Egypt

easy.question: Who called Abram and questioned him about his actions?
easy.explanation: Verse 18 says: “And Pharaoh called Abram.”

easy.question: What did Pharaoh command Abram to do?
easy.explanation: Pharaoh returned Sarai to Abram and said: “Take her, and go thy way.”

easy.question: What happened to Pharaoh and his house?
answers: They were afflicted with great plagues
easy.explanation: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues.

medium.question: Why were Pharaoh and his house afflicted with plagues?
medium.explanation: The verse connects the plagues with the fact that Sarai was Abram’s wife.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Pharaoh sent Abram away, questioned him, and then took Sarai
Pharaoh was afflicted, called Abram, returned Sarai, and sent them away
Abram returned Sarai, and then Pharaoh was afflicted and called him
medium.explanation: First the plagues came; then Pharaoh questioned Abram, returned Sarai, and sent them away.

medium.question: What does “plagues” mean in “the Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues”?
medium.explanation: The word refers to severe afflictions that struck Pharaoh and his household.

challenge.question: Why was Pharaoh angry with Abram and asked why he had not told him that Sarai was his wife?
answers: Because Pharaoh took Sarai as a wife based on Abram’s claim that she was his sister
Because Abram refused to give him gifts
Because Sarai left Pharaoh’s palace without permission
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh realized that Abram’s statement had led him to take a married woman.

challenge.question: What can be understood from Pharaoh’s command to his men to send Abram, Sarai, and all that he had away?
answers: Pharaoh wanted Abram to remain in the palace
Pharaoh wanted them removed from Egypt quickly
Pharaoh wanted to take all of Abram’s possessions
challenge.explanation: Sending all of them away, together with everything Abram owned, shows that Pharaoh wanted them to leave Egypt.

challenge.question: What does Pharaoh’s response show about his understanding of the situation?
answers: He thought Sarai was still Abram’s sister
He did not know who Sarai was
He understood that Sarai was Abram’s wife and returned her to him
challenge.explanation: Pharaoh explicitly says that she is Abram’s wife and commands Abram to take her and leave.

answers: Because Pharaoh took Sarai as a wife based on Abram’s claim that she was his sister
Because Abram refused to give him gifts
Because Sarai left Pharaoh’s palace without permission
questions.explanation: Pharaoh realized that Abram’s statement had led him to take a married woman.

answers: Pharaoh wanted Abram to remain in the palace

Pharaoh wanted to take all of Abram’s possessions
questions.explanation: Sending all of them away, together with everything Abram owned, shows that Pharaoh wanted them to leave Egypt.

answers: He thought Sarai was still Abram’s sister

He understood that Sarai was Abram’s wife and returned her to him
